pool.text: French traders founded Fort Rouillé at the current Exhibition grounds location.
The British established the town of York as the capital of Upper Canada.
The town of York was the site of the Battle of York.
The University of Toronto was established as the first institution of higher education.
York was renamed and incorporated as the City of Toronto.
Slavery was banned outright in Upper Canada and throughout the British Empire.
The Toronto Coach Terminal began serving as the city intercity hub.
The Toronto Stock Exchange had become the largest in the country.
The City of Toronto and 12 surrounding municipalities were federated into Metropolitan Toronto.
Lawrence Seaway gave ships access to the Great Lakes from the Atlantic Ocean.
The first Caribana took place when the Caribbean community celebrated Canada's Centennial.
The world's tallest freestanding structure was completed at a height of 553.33 metres.
The city previously hosted the Summer Paralympics events in this year.
The Wychwood Park neighbourhood was designated as an Ontario Heritage Conservation district.
Toronto hosted the Grand Prix of Toronto as part of IndyCar.
The record year for murders was previously noted with 89 total.
The Toronto Raptors basketball team entered the NBA and earned playoff spots.
Voters opposed a municipal merger proposal in referendums held in March.
Toronto became the centre of Canada's principal outbreak of severe acute respiratory syndrome.
The Northeast blackout interrupted electricity, public transit, and traffic signals throughout the city.
